bounded_slice.leaf: branch-deletion commit-SHA replayability and persistent-verification recovery
bounded_slice.method: First-party GitHub documentation only; one bounded documentation audit, no destructive experiment and no second leaf.
bounded_slice.tested_scope: Whether a commit referenced only by SHA can be treated as durably retrievable/replayable after its ordinary containing branch is deleted, and whether GitHub persistent signature verification can be recovered without external backup services, artifact/LFS/package quotas, manual restoration, protected execution, paid/finite quota, or hidden executor; subsequent repository-network changes remain part of the durability criterion.

observations.observation: GitHub documents that when the branch containing a commit was deleted or force-pushed, recovery is to have a collaborator who still has the commit locally push it to a new branch, then fetch that recovered branch. The documentation does not promise indefinite GitHub-side retrieval of an otherwise unreferenced object by SHA after branch deletion.

The REST 'Get a commit' endpoint accepts a commit SHA as the ref. This establishes SHA-addressed retrieval when the commit object remains available to the repository, but it is an access mechanism rather than an object-retention guarantee.

GitHub stores a persistent verification record alongside a verified commit and reuses that record when the same commit appears again in the same repository network. The record is explicitly scoped to that repository network.

inferences: A bare commit SHA is not, by first-party documentation alone, a zero-dependency durability guarantee after ordinary branch deletion. GitHub's documented recovery path depends on another extant copy of the commit and a push operation, which would be a manual/external restoration dependency if the scheduled-Chat mechanism itself has no independently retained copy.

The REST commit endpoint gives a narrow partial pass only while the object is still retrievable in the repository; the documentation does not justify extrapolating this to indefinite retention of unreachable commits.

If the exact commit is reintroduced into the same repository network, GitHub's persistent verification record can be reused, so verification recovery has a same-network conditional path. That path does not solve the stronger requirement because reintroduction requires the commit bytes to exist somewhere and the verification record is not documented as portable across a later repository-network split.

Therefore the exact tested mechanism fails the branch-deletion-plus-network-change durability gate as a self-contained scheduled-Chat evidence handoff. It remains a partial pass for currently retained objects and same-network verification reuse only.
uncertainty: No destructive branch-deletion experiment was executed.

GitHub may retain some unreachable objects operationally for some period, but the cited public documentation does not provide a retention duration or an indefinite retrievability guarantee; this run therefore does not treat undocumented retention as acceptance evidence.

The result is limited to GitHub-hosted commit retrieval and GitHub persistent signature-verification records; it does not generalize to independent cryptographic evidence packages that store the full object payload elsewhere.

hard_gates.conflict_check: No O/O-derived, downstream, other-worker semantic input, shared ledger, or scheduler mutation was used. Repository APIs were transport only; semantic evidence was first-party GitHub documentation plus prior own role-local state.

continuation: Next invocation re-bootstrap/freeze authority and reconstruct p1-sa-605. Execute exactly one bounded scientist-agents leaf on a self-contained evidence-package redesign that avoids reliance on GitHub retaining an unreachable commit object: test whether storing the minimal replay payload and provenance directly as ordinary role-local repository content (not artifact/LFS/package storage, no external backup, no manual restoration) can make replay survive branch/reference loss while preserving commit/object identity claims without hidden execution. Distinguish 'replay the evidence package' from 'resurrect the original Git object in GitHub'; preserve zero finite quota, zero incremental cost, CLEAN boundaries, exact tested scope, and no second leaf.
